explanations.answer: Oversee the work of the LORD's house
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. David says, "24,000 are to oversee the work of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 23:4). That's more than half of the 38,000. Somebody has to keep the whole operation running, and it takes a crowd.

Walls are a fine job, but they're not on David's list here. He says the biggest group, 24,000 men, is to "oversee the work of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 23:4). The work is about the LORD's house, not the city's walls. Easy one to mix up when you're picturing a big crew.

Nobody's knocking on doors for money in this passage, friend. David says 24,000 are "to oversee the work of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 23:4). The officers and judges are a smaller group of 6,000. Tax collector isn't on the list at all.
You got it, baker. David says 4,000 "are to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise" (1 Chronicles 23:5). That's a whole band. I'd love to hear that rehearsal.

Guarding is close to the gatekeeper job, but the treasury isn't mentioned here. The last 4,000 are "to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise" (1 Chronicles 23:5). The gatekeepers were their own group of 4,000. Four groups, four jobs, and this one's all music.

No drills and no marching in this list, friend. David says the last group of 4,000 is "to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise" (1 Chronicles 23:5). Their job is praise, and they use instruments for it. Not a sword in sight.
That's right, baker. David says the instruments are ones "I have made for giving praise" (1 Chronicles 23:5). He's the king, and he's the one talking. He made them with praise in mind.

Solomon is David's son, and David just installed him as king (1 Chronicles 23:1). But he isn't the one who made these instruments. The one speaking in verse 5 says, "the instruments I have made for giving praise," and that speaker is David.

Aaron, Moses' brother, does show up later in this passage, set apart for holy work (1 Chronicles 23:13). But the instruments aren't his. In verse 5 David is the one talking, and he says, "the instruments I have made for giving praise." I'd say that's a pretty good hint.

Baked just right on the memory, friend. David says, "So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service" (1 Chronicles 23:26). The reason he gives is that the LORD "has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever" (1 Chronicles 23:25). I think those Levites were happy to put down the heavy stuff.

Guarding is a real job in this passage, since 4,000 Levites are gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 23:5). But the verse says something different. David says the Levites "no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service" (1 Chronicles 23:26). Carrying is the job that's done.

Nothing about repairs here, friend. David says, "So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service" (1 Chronicles 23:26). The word is carry. The tabernacle was a tent, so I bet moving it was the big chore, but that part is my guess.

That's right. The Levites' duty was "to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 23:28). Aaron's family was set apart for the most holy things (1 Chronicles 23:13). So the Levites were the helpers, and every good kitchen has them.

Moses, the man of God, does have family in this passage. His sons Gershom and Eliezer are named (1 Chronicles 23:14-15). But the text says the Levites were to assist "the descendants of Aaron" (1 Chronicles 23:28). Aaron and Moses were brothers, so it's an easy mix-up.

The leaders were at the big meeting David called (1 Chronicles 23:2), so I see why you picked them. But the Levites' duty was "to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD" (1 Chronicles 23:28). That's who they were helping.
Flip that one around, friend. The text says the Levites were responsible for "the courts and chambers" (1 Chronicles 23:28). They weren't told to stay out. They were told to look after them.

Right, it's false. The Levites were to be "responsible for the courts and chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God" (1 Chronicles 23:28). They're in charge of those places, not kept out of them. Think of it as having the keys.

Yes, baker! The list includes "the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size" (1 Chronicles 23:29). Measuring is on there too. I'm just glad somebody in the Bible knows you can't eyeball the flour.

No farming on this list, friend. After the showbread, the flour and the wafers, the job list adds "the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size" (1 Chronicles 23:29). It starts at the flour and works from there. The fields aren't part of it.

No bread stand here. The job list says "the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size" (1 Chronicles 23:29). The bread was for the service of the LORD's house. Nobody's working a cash register.

That's it. The Levites "were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening" (1 Chronicles 23:30). Twice a day, every day. That's a steady habit of thanks.

explanations.answer: Once a week on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: The Sabbath does come up, but not for this. The Levites were to stand "every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening" (1 Chronicles 23:30). The Sabbath shows up in the next verse, with the burnt offerings (1 Chronicles 23:31). The daily praise happens way more often than weekly.

The feasts are mentioned, friend, in the verse about burnt offerings (1 Chronicles 23:31). But the thanks and praise happen on a much tighter schedule. They were to stand "every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening" (1 Chronicles 23:30).

True, baker! The verse says, "So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place" (1 Chronicles 23:32). They also served the house of the LORD under their brothers, the descendants of Aaron. That's a good wrap-up for a long list.

Not quite, friend. The last verse says, "So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place" (1 Chronicles 23:32). So the statement is true. They also served the house of the LORD under the descendants of Aaron.
